bull_case_summary: VT offers broad global index participation at 0.06% expenses. Round two retains quantified US/technology concentration while showing meaningful non-US and other-sector breadth, making allocation fit rather than breakout evidence the basis for strategic buying.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts the breadth and long-horizon allocation case. It retains correlated drawdown exposure at 61.9% US and 33.3% technology weights, without inventing an October NAV premium or treating July portfolio P/E as current fair value.
key_points_of_agreement: Low costs have structural utility without promising returns.
Missing tactical alpha does not defeat disciplined allocation ownership.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether increasing exposure fits an actual allocation need and drawdown capacity, which are outside this research envelope.
unresolved_uncertainties: October NAV premium/discount and any tactical valuation advantage.
Personal allocation fit and tolerance of correlated global-equity loss.
